tests.name: Quick Check
tests.description: Timed check on Vocabulary & English Derivatives

questions.question: Q: What is the Defined Vocabulary List and why is it important?
questions.correctAnswer: The DVL is the official list of Latin words that may appear in the GCSE translation papers. Words outside the DVL are glossed in exams. It contains approximately 400-500 words that must be memorised.

questions.question: Q: Give three English derivatives from Latin verbs and their meanings.
questions.correctAnswer: Videre (to see) → video; scribere (to write) → scribble, scribe, script; audire (to hear) → audible, audience; dicere (to say) → dictate, diction; facere (to make/do) → factory, fact (any three).

questions.question: Q: What English derivatives come from aqua, luna, and terra?
questions.correctAnswer: Aqua (water) → aquatic, aqueduct, aquarium. Luna (moon) → lunar, lunatic. Terra (earth) → terrestrial, territory, terrain.

tests.name: Exam-Style Practice
tests.description: Short-answer practice on Vocabulary & English Derivatives

questions.question: Q: Name five common Latin prefixes with their English meanings and a derivative.
questions.correctAnswer: Trans- (across) → transport, translate. Sub- (under) → submarine, subordinate. Pre- (before) → predict, prefix. Re- (back/again) → return, revisit. Ex/e- (out of) → export, eject (any five).

questions.question: Q: What do the Latin abbreviations i.e., e.g., and N.B. stand for?
questions.correctAnswer: i.e. = id est (that is); e.g. = exempli gratia (for the sake of example); N.B. = nota bene (note well).

questions.question: Q: Give the Latin roots behind the English words 'audible', 'dictation', and 'manuscript'.
questions.correctAnswer: Audible from audire (to hear). Dictation from dicere (to say). Manuscript from manus (hand) + scribere (to write) — written by hand.

questions.question: Q: Name five of the most common Latin verbs on the DVL.
questions.correctAnswer: Sum (to be), habeo (to have), dico (to say), facio (to make/do), venio (to come), video (to see), mitto (to send), capio (to take), ago (to do/drive), pono (to place) (any five).

questions.question: Q: Why is learning Latin vocabulary through derivatives an effective strategy?
questions.correctAnswer: It creates memory links: knowing that 'portare' means 'to carry' makes it easy to remember transport, portable, porter, export, import, and support. Derivatives provide English-language hooks for each Latin word.
